data.narrative:
AlixLabs is a Series A-stage semiconductor company founded by Jonas Sundqvist, Dmitry Suyatin, and Amin Karimi, having raised €15M to date. The valuation universe comprises 11 private peers in Chips & Semiconductors (including SambaNova Systems, Cerebras, and Credo Semiconductor) and 3 public comparables (ALAB, NVDA, AMD).

Of three valuation methods tested, only stage-progression proved applicable. Using the €15M total raised as a proxy for current value and applying a 2.0x multiplier typical of Series A-to-next-stage progression yields an implied valuation of €30M. Peer-median analysis was not viable; while 12 same-sector peers exist, filtering for matching stage and valuation tier produced insufficient datapoints (fewer than 3 required). Public-comp anchoring was skipped due to absent revenue disclosure—standard for private companies—though the public semiconductor universe carries a median P/S of 21.0x.

The analysis supports a valuation range of €26M to €34M, centered on €30M. This range reflects moderate confidence in a single methodological input. Key uncertainties include the representativeness of the 2.0x step-up multiplier for AlixLabs' specific profile, the lack of peer-set triangulation, and the absence of revenue data that would enable public-market anchoring. Investors should weight this estimate accordingly pending disclosure of financial metrics or tighter peer comparables.
